Hi Amit/Claire —

Thanks again for the time today. Short recap + proposed next steps so we have shared clarity.

Key pain points you emphasized:
- Unpredictable latency spikes during peak billing-window queries (even for short prompts).
- Cost constraints: need predictable unit economics for triage & claims workflows.
- Regulatory requirement: audit logs and per-request data retention controls for PHI-adjacent metadata.

Goals we heard:
- 95th-pct latency for common completions (<=64 tokens) under 200ms in production.
- Throughput to support sustained peaks ~180 req/s with burst to 400 req/s during billing windows.
- Ops-ready rollout with canary + automatic fallback to cheaper/quantized variants.

Attachments: Solstice-MAP-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — mutual action plan draft; SLA-draft-Solstice-20290514.pdf (draft SLA)

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Your team to share a 24-hour traffic sample (anonymized) + three representative prompt sets by EOD Thu 5/16.
2) We’ll schedule a 60–90m engineering deep-dive next week (propose Wed 5/22) — Karthik to lead topology & SLOs.
3) Redwood will stand up a 72-hour load test (staging) once sample traffic is received — goal: validate 95th-pct latency and cost envelope.

If this summary looks right, please confirm and add anyone from procurement who should be looped in (I included a placeholder line in the MAP).

Thanks —

—Marissa Cole

Hi Amit/Claire —

Appreciate the quick follow-up. Short technical alignment and what we would validate during the staging run.

1) Scope and SLO definitions (proposed):
- Latency: 95th-pct end-to-end <= 160ms for responses <= 64 tokens (measured at Redwood ingress), 99th-pct <= 350ms.
- Throughput: sustain 180 req/s for 8-hour windows with ability to burst to 400 req/s for up to 10 minutes.
- Error budget: <0.1% request failures (5xx) per day.
- Cold starts: treat separately — we guarantee warm-path SLOs; cold-starts count toward a separate metric and are excluded from primary 95th-pct SLO until warmup period in rollout.

2) Model & performance constraints:
- Candidate families: redwood-instruct-v2-13b (8-bit quant), llama-2-70b-q4f16 (for higher-fidelity baselines), and Redwood-v1-chat-13b (for constrained cost cases).
- Context window: require 4k tokens; architecture should support KV-cache sharding to optimize long-context reuse.
- Quantization: recommend 8-bit or q4 variants for production; 4-bit can be evaluated for cost but expect some regen/quality delta on clinical prompts.

3) Deployment topology recommendation:
- Dedicated U.S. region (us-east1) GPU pool behind multi-variant router.
- Two active model variants: primary (redwood-instruct-v2-13b-8bit) + fallback (redwood-instruct-v2-13b-q4f16) with automated fallback on CPU/GPU pressure.
- Edge prefix caching: prefix/KV cache at the router layer for common prompts (estimated token reuse > 35% for triage flows).
- Autoscaling policy: target CPU/GPU utilization 70% with conservative cooldown (3m) and burst capacity throttle for billing windows.
- Canary plan: 10% traffic → 30% → 100% over 48h, validate key health metrics and latency delta at each step.

4) Staging run plan (72 hours):
- Input: anonymized 24h traffic × 3 (to emulate 72-hour profile) with an engineered burst at hour 48.
- Metrics to collect: per-route p50/p95/p99, token cost, KV cache hit rate, tail latencies by prompt length, error categories.
- Success criteria: meet latency SLOs for warm-path; cost within agreed target (TBD after we see traffic sample).

5) Required artifacts from Solstice:
- Anonymized traffic sample (see Marissa’s ask).
- Example prompt sets with expected output length buckets.
- Security questionnaire — we’ll circulate Redwood’s SOC2 artifacts and integration checklist.

Attachments: solstice_technical_appendix.pdf (topology diagrams + test script)

I’ll prepare a minimal staging run plan and timeline once we have the traffic sample. Proposed engineer leads: Karthik (Redwood), Priya Natarajan (Redwood) — I’ll add Priya in the next thread when we schedule the deep-dive.

Thanks,
—Karthik
